description: The Soviet Union successfully launches the first artificial satellite, Sputnik 1, into orbit around the Earth.
The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is established in the United States to coordinate and conduct civilian space exploration activities.
Yuri Gagarin, a Soviet cosmonaut, becomes the first human to travel into space aboard Vostok 1, completing a single orbit around the Earth.
Alan Shepard, an American astronaut, becomes the first American to travel into space aboard the Mercury spacecraft, completing a suborbital flight.
Valentina Tereshkova, a Soviet cosmonaut, becomes the first woman to travel into space aboard Vostok 6, orbiting the Earth 48 times.
Gus Grissom and John Young become the first U.S. astronauts to fly aboard a multi-person spacecraft, Gemini 3, performing three orbits of the Earth.
Alexei Leonov, a Soviet cosmonaut, performs the first-ever spacewalk (extravehicular activity) lasting 12 minutes and 9 seconds.
Apollo 8, a U.S. manned spacecraft, becomes the first manned mission to orbit the Moon and return safely to Earth.
The Soviet Union launches Salyut 1, the world's first space station, paving the way for long-duration human space missions.
The Apollo-Soyuz Test Project marks the first international human spaceflight mission, with a U.S. Apollo spacecraft docking with a Soviet Soyuz spacecraft in Earth orbit.
The Voyager program launches two spacecraft, Voyager 1 and Voyager 2, on a mission to study the outer Solar System and beyond.
The Soviet Union launches Mir, a modular space station, which becomes the world's first consistently inhabited long-term research facility in space.
The U.S. space shuttle Challenger explodes shortly after launch, resulting in the loss of all seven crew members.
The Hubble Space Telescope, a space-based observatory, is launched by the Space Shuttle Discovery, revolutionizing astronomical observations.
NASA's Mars Pathfinder mission successfully lands a robotic rover, Sojourner, on the surface of Mars, providing valuable data about the planet.
The first component of the International Space Station (ISS), Zarya, is launched into orbit, beginning the assembly of the largest human-made structure in space.
NASA's twin Mars rovers, Spirit and Opportunity, land successfully on Mars, conducting scientific exploration of the planet's surface.
NASA's New Horizons spacecraft successfully completes a flyby of Pluto, providing detailed images and data about the distant dwarf planet.

events: Crewed missions to the International Space Station
description: Ongoing crewed missions to the International Space Station (ISS) continue, with astronauts from multiple countries participating in scientific research and space exploration.
SpaceX's Falcon Heavy rocket is successfully launched, becoming the most powerful operational rocket in the world.
NASA announces the Artemis program, aiming to return humans to the Moon by 2024 and establish sustainable lunar exploration.
NASA's Perseverance rover successfully lands on Mars, embarking on a mission to search for signs of ancient microbial life and collect samples for future return to Earth.

events: Upcoming James Webb Space Telescope launch
description: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), a powerful successor to the Hubble Space Telescope, is scheduled for launch to observe the universe in infrared wavelengths.
Plans and initiatives continue to be developed for future manned missions to Mars, with the goal of further exploring and potentially colonizing the Red Planet.
